messages:
sam: quick idea — instead of a fixed token-bucket refill, what if we use an adaptive 'delta window' that temporarily increases refill during short high-variance bursts and decays back to baseline?

sam: motivation: some frontends do 1s UI bursts (typing+submit) that look like microspikes. fixed buckets either punish them or force a large steady allowance which wastes capacity. delta window adapts for short windows only.

olivia: can you sketch how it behaves? curious about worst-case for sustained load.

sam: sketch: maintain a short-window interarrival variance (sigma_short) and long-window avg rate (r_long). when sigma_short >> baseline, allow a temporary multiplier m = 1 + clamp((sigma_short / sigma_base) - 1, 0, max_bump). refill_rate = r_long * m for window T_delta, then exponentially decay m -> 1 with tau. basically token bucket refill follows EWMA of burstiness.

sam: pseudo-config:

```
name: adaptive_delta_tokenbucket
base_rate: 100 req/s
burst_max_multiplier: 3.0
short_window: 2s
long_window: 60s
delta_window: 8s
decay_tau: 4s
sensitivity_threshold: 1.5  # sigma ratio
```

lee: hmm. So it's token-bucket at core but refill rate is dynamic. How do we avoid one noisy org gaming it (sustained oscillation)?

ben: my take: need a hysteresis + cap on cumulative allowed extra tokens per org over N minutes. if they sustain, the long_window avg will catch up and m will shrink. but add a budget cap: extra_tokens_allowed_per_minute.

maria: thinking about rollout: console needs to show both instant spike credits and cumulative extra credit usage. ops should be able to toggle per-org sensitivity. prefer feature-flagged canary by org tag.

sam: yes — rollout plan idea:
1) default off for prod, enable in staging + internal orgs
2) run for 48h vs control, capture metrics: p95 latency, throttles/sec, extra_token_rate, error-rate
3) if extra_token_rate correlated w/ bad sustained load, revert or tighten caps

olivia: telemetry-wise we should add: `burst_multiplier`, `delta_window_active`, `extra_tokens_consumed`, and a derived `microburst_allowed_pct` on dashboards. add alert if `extra_tokens_consumed`/minute > threshold for >5m.

infra-bot: rate-limiter: canary config applied to cluster `rl-canary-2` (testing) at 1853502540.

ben: small note on leaky-bucket alternative — leaky buckets smooth output, but they penalize bursty ingress more. combining both helps: leaky out + adaptive token refill in front. gives steady egress while accommodating short spikes.

lee: console UX: show a tiny timeline sparkline next to quota with a hover that explains "shortburst credit: automatic transient allowance to preserve UX; capped and decays". ops can click to see contributing metrics and turn off per-org.

maria: agree. also add a rollout checkbox for "enable delta-window for this org" in org settings + audit log entry.

sam: experiment owner volunteers? i can take metrics/implementation for limiter, olivia can own dashboards, maria can do rollout UX, ben/lee will help on policy caps.

olivia: I can take dashboards. I'll add the new metrics to the per-org quota page and wire thresholds in the incident runbook.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: feature-flag gate created. canary rollout window opens 1853502600 -> 1853503400.

sam: cool — I'll open a PR with the limiter hook and a small simulation test. rough timeline: PR + bench + canary config by EOD tomorrow.

olivia: perfect. :thumbsup:
